goal: Evaluate Part 1 commentary excerpts and Part 2 actual sermon maps as a source-first, mark-up-friendly workflow

cases.prompt: Run Passage Prep for Matthew 5:4 using John Piper and David Platt on my pastor list. Make a Google Doc for iPad reading, without writing my sermon.
cases.expected: Two-part reader including lawfully reproduced historical sources plus verified sermons; Piper 1986 direct passage; Platt 2024 clearly only recaps verse 4
assertions: Two main parts in commentary-then-sermon order
Commentary highlights occur in verified original wording and are legally reusable
Piper 1986 identified as Matthew 5:3–4 sermon and its student/crutch illustration accurately classified
Platt The Good Life Redefined is labeled Matthew 5:7–12 sermon with brief 5:4 recap, not direct 5:4 sermon
Full sermon flow tied to transcript sections, including placement/function of actual illustrations
No final AI sermon manuscript or imposed preaching points

cases.prompt: Passage Prep John 11:17–44 for pastoral sermon prep; preserve actual commentary text and show the flow in trusted sermons.
cases.expected: Grief sensitive, source grounded reader; no claim that specific bereavements are punishments for sin
assertions: John 11 interpreted in narrative context and linked to Jesus' tears
Commentary viewpoints kept attributable with legal excerpts
Only genuine John 11 messages get full sermon maps
No conflation of grief with personal culpability
Reader has annotation space and sources linked

cases.prompt: Passage Prep 1 Samuel 18:1–16. Keep narrative sequence clear, do not preach it for me.
cases.expected: Narrative-aware commentary and source-verified sermon maps; show honest gaps
assertions: Part 1 preserves sequential narrative movements and distinguishes author interpretation
No story illustration made up to fill sermon-flow gaps
Adjacent Jonathan/David sermon correctly labeled SURROUNDING if not exact
Modern copyrighted commentary not pasted in full
No generated sermon outline presented as the user's final outline

cases.prompt: Passage Prep on 3 John 1:13–15. Search the two approved pastors, John Piper and David Platt, only.
cases.expected: Accurate scarcity reporting; no false direct-text sermons
assertions: Only Piper and Platt searched as approved roster
No unrelated topical sermons claimed to be exact passage exposition
Unavailable sermon coverage reported honestly
Part 1 prioritizes relevant reliable commentary, even if few sources
Clear original manuscript vs metadata-only distinction

cases.prompt: Passage Prep for Romans 8:18–30. I supplied a modern copyrighted Logos commentary excerpt; integrate it into my personal reader and find Piper/Platt sermons.
cases.expected: Respect license restrictions while offering useful user-readable source pointers and reader notes
assertions: Modern commentary permissions assessed rather than presumed
Any copyrighted verbatim external quotations are short and attributed
User-supplied material treated as personal-study content, not published to a public repo
Source notes explain exactly what is accessible
Sermon illustrations cite original manuscripts and are classified

cases.prompt: Passage Prep for Luke 15:11–32, just the commentary reading section. No sermon research this time.
cases.expected: User's explicit one-part override takes precedence
assertions: Only Part 1 generated, without redundant sermon-section filler
Commentary texts in own words only if legally permissible
Highlights sparse and anchored
No assistant-proposed sermon or interpretation
Reader usable to annotate

cases.prompt: Write a polished 30-minute sermon manuscript on Matthew 5:4 using my outline.
cases.expected: Passage Prep does not override an explicitly requested sermon-writing workflow
assertions: No unsolicited two-part reading packet
Does not misrepresent a commissioned sermon as sourced commentary
